name: rasa.module.field-log
description: Portable field-engagement log: one record per customer visit/trip/interaction (drive -> on-site work -> debrief: what we did, how it went, pros/cons, follow-ups), attached to a customer account.

rasa.note: The field-engagement module of the RasaOS business-ops set (leads / schedule / contracts / invoices / field-log). Owns exactly one record — the Visit: drive out -> on-site work -> debrief (what we did, how it went, pros/cons, follow-ups) — across the planned -> completed -> debriefed lifecycle. This is THE PROVEN one: a live consulting/field practice already runs this exact loop by hand (schedule -> drive -> on-site -> debrief), so the record below is a real working shape, not an invented one — which makes field-log the natural FIRST business-ops module to grow real skills. Every visit joins to its customer by the shared account handle @acct-<slug> (the same spine every sibling business-ops module uses); the account's own record lives on the account hub, which RasaOS does not yet have as a first-class primitive (canon task SA-032 — engagement-hub primitive). This module never seeds a competing accounts registry. The one thing that varies per practice — visit types, the debrief template (what 'pros / cons / how it went' means here), travel/mileage policy, and billable-hours policy — lives in a project-owned .claude/field-log-gate.md seam (seeded skip-if-exists), the field-log analogue of module.tasks' done-gate; /debrief hard-stops if the debrief template is unfilled. Cross-module references are SOFT (present-if-mounted, graceful-if-absent, never requires.elements[]): a scheduled booking (rasa.module.schedule) becomes a planned visit; a completed billable visit feeds an invoice line (rasa.module.invoices); a follow-up may cite a rasa.module.tasks TASK-NNN. HONEST SCOPE: v0.1.0 ships the spine (field-log-rules.md), the specification (content/BUILD_PLAN.md), the seam template, and the live-ledger template. The /visit, /debrief, and /field-log skills are the authoring build phase, gated per BUILD_PLAN.md M-1..M-3 and held until a real consumer declares the module in requires.elements[] (the module.tasks extract-after-proof precedent; field-log is expected to be the first of the six to clear that gate).

element.description: Element-owned files mirrored into the install target's .claude/ per canon ELEMENT_CONTRACT.md §7. Refreshed on Element upgrade. The field-log-gate seam and the live ledger are NOT here — they are project-owned (see seed.files).

files.note: The portable field-engagement spine: the Visit record + canonical field set, the planned -> completed -> debriefed lifecycle, the shared @acct-<slug> account spine, the boundary against schedule/invoices, and the ledger conventions. Element-owned; refreshed on upgrade. References .claude/field-log-gate.md for the per-practice slice (visit types, debrief template, travel + billable policy); it hardcodes none of it.
Describes what this module ships and how it installs. Fork/author-time doc; not installed into consumer projects.

The v0.1.0 specification + build plan (the Visit entity model, the planned/completed/debriefed lifecycle, the field-log-gate seam, the deferred /visit /debrief /field-log skills gated per extract-after-proof, the soft cross-refs, and the honest scope). Author-time doc; not installed into consumer projects.

seed.description: One-time, project-owned files copied at install only (skip-if-exists), per canon ELEMENT_CONTRACT.md §7. These belong to the consuming project after install and are never overwritten on Element upgrade — the project's field-log-gate adapter seam and its live visit ledger.

files.note: The per-practice adapter seam — the four things that vary per field practice: visit types, the debrief template (the sentiment scale + debrief prompts — what 'pros / cons / how it went' means here), travel/mileage policy, and billable-hours policy. Project-owned; the practice fills it. /debrief hard-stops until the debrief template is set. Ships with honest defaults + commented examples; placeholder-free per the documented skip-if-exists policy gap.

The live visit ledger — one entry per customer visit, ordered, carrying the full Visit record (account/date/purpose/attendees/travel/onsite_hours/what-we-did/covered/outcome/sentiment/pros/cons/followups/billable). Project-owned; grows over the practice's life. /visit appends + advances, /debrief fills the how-it-went half. Follow-ups close in place. Account-id bullets (@acct-<slug>) are the shared spine; TASK-NNN / invoice / booking ids are soft references to sibling modules.

Stamped with the Element HEAD commit SHA at init time. Lockfile shape per canon Spec §6 (Connection Contract). When co-installed under a parent that also stamps a lockfile, the parent's is authoritative (single-writer-per-path). Substitutes {{ELEMENT_NAME}}, {{ELEMENT_KIND}}, {{ELEMENT_VERSION}}, {{ELEMENT_REPO}}, {{ELEMENT_BRANCH}}, {{ELEMENT_SHA}}, {{TODAY}} via bin/init.
